sentences.text: The learned Court below vide its order dated 23.09.2024 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
3.

When she shouted, one Janmenjaya Behera of her village came there and rescued her.
On seeing him, the accused fled away from the spot.

She has further alleged that on 28.04.2024, her husband was missing somewhere,
she suspected that the present petitioner might have kidnapped her husband to take revenge.

Hence, she reported at the P.S.
4.
I have perused the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of the Cr. P.C.
She has stated that the petitioner has forcibly committed sexual assault on her.

At the time of the incident,
one of her relative reached the spot by hearing the shouting.
She asked help of one Janmenjaya Behera, who reached the spot and on his intervention she got escaped.

The said eye witness Janmenjaya Behera was examined as P.W.2, who in his testimony has stated as under:
"1.
I know the informant-cum-victim.
I know the accused.
I do not know anything about this case.
I was not examined by the police.

CROSS EXAMINATION:-
2. There was land dispute between the parties.
There was Gandagola between the parties for which the accused had filed a case against the informant and others.
So, the informant filed this case against him."

5. Mr. Sahu, learned counsel for the petitioner has also taken me to the medical evidence, relevant part of the same reads as under:
"5. No forcible sexual intercourse signs found though forcible sexual intercourse cannot be ruled out as the incident took place 42 days back and injuries might have healed.
6. She had her last intercourse with her husband 2 days after the incident."
6. On perusal of the medical evidence, it reveals that the victim had lastly had sexual intercourse with her husband two days after the incident.
Therefore, the conclusive medical evidence could not come to the fore.
7. Mr. Jena, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State submits that the allegations are very specific and the prosecutrix has not been examined yet.
Therefore, he opposes the bail.

8. Regard being had to the testimony of the sole eye witness to the incident and nature of evidence brought on record by the prosecution and the period of custody of the petitioner, i.e. from 01.05.2024, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
